nodes.label: Playground
nodes.rationale: Three-pane free-exploration surface (Palette | Stage | Code): drag, resize, switch managers, read live compilable Java. The one dense, bold region; everything around it stays quiet.

nodes.label: Challenges
nodes.rationale: Graded-practice surface with three deterministic exercise modes, tagged by Bloom difficulty (Recall to Apply to Analyze). Graded by tree/rectangle comparison, never pixels or AI.

nodes.label: Parsons Mode (order the code)
nodes.rationale: Order shuffled Java code magnets to build a target UI. Target derived by executing magnets in canonical order (never stored as pixels); grader executes statement-by-statement with true Swing semantics and reports the first divergence.

nodes.label: Reflow Mode (predict the reflow)
nodes.rationale: Drag a ghost to the predicted post-resize position; grading compares ghost center to the engine-computed rectangle within tolerance (default +/-24px), then animates the true reflow and states the rule.

nodes.label: Reverse Mode (rebuild the target)
nodes.rationale: Rebuild a shown target frame; graded on structural tree equivalence (same comparison Parsons uses) with a deterministic diff naming missing/extra components or wrong settings. No score-shaming, just the next thing to fix.

nodes.label: BorderLayout
nodes.rationale: 5-region resolver (NORTH/SOUTH/EAST/WEST/CENTER); NORTH/SOUTH keep preferred height, EAST/WEST keep preferred width, CENTER absorbs the remainder. Shows only the last component added to each region.

nodes.label: FlowLayout
nodes.rationale: Row-wrapping packer: left-to-right, rows wrap at frame width; align (LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT) plus hgap/vgap knobs.

nodes.label: GridLayout
nodes.rationale: Uniform-cell sizer: all cells same size, ignores component preferred sizes; rows/cols with mutual-zero guard, cell count auto-derives.

nodes.label: Deterministic Code Generation
nodes.rationale: Compilable vanilla javax.swing/java.awt Java regenerated on every action; deterministic variable naming by type+counter; diff-flash traces this-action-to-this-code. Never approximated, never LLM-generated, so students can copy it straight into an IDE.

nodes.label: One Engine, Two Consumers (single source of truth)
nodes.rationale: layoutTree renders the Playground AND backs every grader, so a challenge can never be correct-on-screen-but-marked-wrong and feedback points at a rule rather than a pixel delta. Growth is additive: each new capability compounds across both surfaces.

nodes.label: Hint Strip (tutor voice)
nodes.rationale: Context-aware aria-live line beneath the canvas doing three jobs: one-time manager tip on switch, selection feedback, and the vanish explanation. The tutor voice names a rule rather than acting like a chatty assistant.

nodes.label: The vanish explanation
nodes.rationale: LayoutLab's single most important teaching moment: when a second component is added to an occupied BorderLayout region Swing hides the first; instead of a silent mystery the strip leads with the rule (BorderLayout shows only the last component added to each region) and shows a chip per hidden component. Error messages are pedagogy.
